title: Booker T. Washington school band and Joe Jones's big band
summary: Ford and Melvin Lastie formed a swing band from the Booker T. Washington band, rehearsing at Corpus Christi. He also met Kid Sheik and played an early job with him.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Yeah. And he and I were in Booker T. Washington's band, and we made up, all of Booker T. Washington's band made up a swing band. We got Hogan, he was dead, a drummer. He didn't have a set of drums. He had to borrow a bass drum from somebody, and he had a snare drum, stands. And I had alto sax and another guy named Fuzzy, he was playing alto, he was in the band also. Who's that? Melvin Lastic. Louis Sergin is his name, he's not in New Orleans now, he went to California. But he and I played alto sax. Joe Jones was a piano player. And which he later on made a rock and roll hit you talk too much. He does talk too much. But at this time he was just going to school. He wasn't in the band, because they didn't use the piano. He was a veteran that came back from the Navy and was going to school on the GI Bill. Sheik was going there too around that time. He was an older guy but he was going to Booker T. Washington. And that's where I first met him. And so we got up a school band together and we played. We got some arrangements, some stop arrangements. And we started playing the voices. The first job we played was, one of them was Corpus Christi used to let us use the auditorium rehearsal. And we used to walk up there from Booker T. Washington to Corpus Christi every day. And that's a good way. All the guys, we used to leave Booker T. Washington, I used to go home first and meet him at 6 o'clock. And we'd be down there every day we'd rehearse. Because Dukey Chase had a band and we wanted to be as good a band as Dukey Chase, because we were the number two band, which we didn't get the name that they did. Well he had the better players and all. But he had a good band. But later on the band built up until the guys got out of school, which was Joe Jones, was the first big band I played. And after I played with the Adams, one of the first jobs I played when I got to saxophone was with Sheik. I'd say about the second job I played indoors. Because he was playing the Sheik of Arabita and as simple as it is I didn't know it. So my uncle had sent one of his sons, Martin, to play also with two trumpets and one saxophone, which was myself. But Sheik was very nice. I felt he was almost like a member of the family. He said that's all right. So my uncle told him, you know, I didn't know too many names but I would make out. So he said that's all right. And she was a trio. We went to Burris and we played and that's about the dirty job I played.
